text:
infra-bot: SEV2 alert: multiple serve-runtime pods in us-west-2 reporting OOM / container crash + node bounce. Crashloop count=6 across nodes gpu-a-*/gpu-b-* :warning:

alice: seeing gradual increase in mem RSS on kv-cache allocator over last 48h, looks like slow creep not sudden spike

ben: confirmed. traces show paged-attention allocator fragmentation — resident pages not reclaimed, compaction not triggering

carla: customer impact? any 5xx spikes?

dan: Grafana: 5xx rate up 2.3x for realtime endpoints, latency spike p95 -> 1.6s. Few customers saw request failures, support already got 3 tickets.

alice: stack: serve-runtime v2.4.1, allocator build with ATT_PAGED=1, KV_CACHE_MAX=12GB present for these nodes

ben: logs contain repeated CUDA errors before OOM: `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` then container killed by OOM-killer

alice: snippet from pod logs:

```

E1023 04:12:07.123456 1 allocator.cc:742] attention_paged: page map inconsistency at slot=0x7f9b... val=0x0
E1023 04:12:07.123458 1 gpu_driver.cc:328] cudaErrorIllegalAddress: kernel launch failed
Killed
```

carla: ok. likely memory corruption or stale page pointer triggering illegal access then leak leads to OOM. Any recent deploys?

deploy-bot: Deploy event: serve-runtime v2.4.1 rolled to us-west-2 at 2026-03-14T22:30Z by @ben (rollout-id: r-20260314-55) :rocket:

ben: yes rolled ~12h ago. But logs show fragmentation pattern predating deploy, slower slope. could be workload change + rollout exposing it.

alice: immediate mitigation idea: 1) reduce KV_CACHE_MAX to 6GB on nodes in the pool, 2) enable aggressive eviction flag, 3) scale down concurrency / batch size for realtime route. We can patch via k8s config map and do rolling restart canary.

dan: supportability: will need customer communication if we restrict throughput for affected customers. recommend throttle only internal lanes first.

carla: medical checklist for oncall handoff: who will own mitigation steps now? I can take triage and coordinate restarts.

alice: I will apply config changes and do one-canary restart. ben pls stand by for tracing and kernel logs collection.

ben: on it. collecting nvml snapshots and dmesg across nodes. nvml shows steadily increasing reserved mem in page pools, and free fragments not coalescing.

alice: patch we're going to apply (kubectl snippet):

```
kubectl -n runtime set env ds/serve-runtime KV_CACHE_MAX=6GB KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.65 ATTN_PAGED_COMPACT=1
kubectl -n runtime rollout restart ds/serve-runtime --selector=zone=us-west-2 --timeout=10m
```

ben: will also hotpatch runtime to short-circuit paged freed-list: `--kv-force-defrag` for canary nodes only.

carla: make sure metrics alert suppression is in place to avoid noise during restarts. I'll mute pager for the alert rule for 30m.

alice: launching canary now on node gpu-a-3, will watch 5xx and mem RSS.

[3m later]

alice: canary restarted ✅ memory RSS dropped from 10.9GB -> 5.8GB on the new pod, no immediate cuda errors after restart. tracing shows fewer page allocations.

ben: collecting heap profile from both pre- and post- restart. attaching snippet of kv stats:

```
pre: kv_slots_alloc=1.2M kv_free_fragments=234k kv_fragmented_bytes=3.8GB
post: kv_slots_alloc=650k kv_free_fragments=58k kv_fragmented_bytes=1.1GB
```

carla: good metrics. begin gradual rollout to remaining nodes with 3 node canary batches. escalate to SRE if node bounce rate > 2 within 15m.

eve: note: support ticket 10293 from Acme corp shows error trace matching `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` and correlates with 22:10-22:45 window. I've messaged customer with ETA.

dan: cost note: reducing KV cache may increase token cost by ~8% for affected workloads. ops ok with that for short term.

alice: rolling to next batch now. will keep small pause between batches to observe reclaim behavior and dmesg.

[10m later]

ben: two nodes in batch B had container crash after restart, both showed hardware NIC flaps immediately prior to crash. marking those nodes for replacement. scheduling drain.

carla: moving nodes with hardware flaps out of pool. continuing rollouts on stable nodes only.

alice: after full rollout to stable cohort (8 nodes) we see 5xx down to baseline, mem RSS stabilized at targeted KV_CACHE_MAX ranges, no cuda errors in last 20m.

carla: customer impact assessment: ~0.6% requests failed across global customers, 3 escalations opened, one SLO miss recorded. recommend post-incident follow-up and customer update.

ben: created ticket BUG-1234: paged-attn allocator fragmentation + stale free-list pointer leading to illegal memory access and slow leak. assign to eng-runtime (ben, alice).

alice: next steps: deeper root cause analysis on stale pointer path, add defensive checks in allocator, and improved compaction heuristics. plan for hotfix 2.4.2 with additional unit tests.

carla: oncall handoff: I'm handing off to @eve at 08:00 PST. Documented mitigation and current state: rollouts complete to stable nodes, remaining flagged nodes drained for hardware replacement, monitoring watch for 2h.

eve: taking over. I'll keep watch and validate no regressions. thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Rollout complete: serve-runtime config patch rolled to 8 nodes in us-west-2 (r-20260314-55-hotfix).

alice: marking thread as incident-handled but will keep follow-up doc for postmortem.

carla: closing pager after 2h observation if stable. filing followup PM notes and customer comms draft.

[end of thread]
